text:
Alyssa: quick follow-up after the RFC review — we need to decide where the policy eval lives (edge vs control plane) and what the runtime contract looks like. TL;DR: prefer simple runtime contract to keep serving fast, but need levers for per-tenant overrides and regional routing.

Chris: +1. main concern is p99 latency if we call control-plane for every request. caching helps but invalidation is messy.

Maria: can we split "decision" types? e.g., routing decisions (region/capacity) cached aggressively, while cost/quality scoring happens async or best-effort.

Sam: agree with Maria. For strict SLOs, routing must be local. Cost-tiering and model selection can be eventual and allow fallback.

Alyssa: proposed layers: (1) Local fast policy: small surface, purely deterministic, cacheable TTLs. (2) Enriched policy from control plane: more features, telemetry, rollouts. (3) Offline policy evals for batch optimization suggestions. Thoughts? :thinking_face: 

Priya: how do we express precedence? tenant overrides > region rules > global defaults? we need a clear deterministic merge order.

Chris: yes. Merge order must be in runtime contract. Also need a compact, typed payload for local eval to avoid pulling full DSL. e.g. {"model_hint":"opt-13b-q4", "latency_budget_ms":120, "cost_tier":"standard"}.

DevX: proposal for runtime contract (very small):
```
{
  "decision_version": "v1",
  "input_signals": ["region","tenant_id","latency_budget_ms","request_priority"],
  "outputs": ["model_variant","route_region","fallback_policy"],
  "cache_ttl_s": 60
}
```
Keep it intentionally tiny so SDKs can evaluate or consult local cache.

Maria: +1 to the tiny contract. two followups: (a) how do we deliver tenant overrides? (b) what happens on cache-miss?

Sam: deliver overrides via signed blob synced to nodes (periodic) or via push when changed. On cache-miss fallback order: local default -> cheaper model in same region -> cross-region route -> degrade to non-streaming. all controlled by fallback_policy in outputs.

Alyssa: security note: signed blobs need rotation and audit logs. also need ability to remotely revoke a tenant override (e.g., compliance).

Priya: what about policy expressivity? We don't want full Turing-complete DSL at edge. Keep a predicate set (range checks, regex on tenant tags, numeric scoring). Complex composition can live in control plane.

Chris: +1. Implementation idea: control plane compiles high-level DSL to a compact bytecode or JSON decision table; edge only executes a small interpreter limited to ops: comparisons, arithmetic, selects. That keeps determinism and small runtime.

DevX: example decision table row: 
`if region=="eu" and latency_budget_ms <= 100 -> route_region=eu, model_variant=fast-quant`
small and readable.

Maria: testing: we need a harness that can run control-plane compiled policies and edge interpreter results side-by-side to ensure parity during rollout. Canary flows should do both and compare outputs.

Sam: telemetry: add a decision_id and control_version to every request log so we can tie outcomes back to policy versions. Helps rollback.

Alyssa: ops concerns: storage for per-node cache, eviction policy, memory footprint. keep TTLs conservative. Also expose a debug endpoint to fetch the evaluated policy for a request id.

Priya: questions on multi-tenant safety: limit number of per-tenant rules evaluated at edge. If a tenant sends many rules, offload to control plane and mark as non-cacheable.

Chris: performance estimate: simple table + interpreter should be sub-200ns per eval on modern CPU if implemented in C++/Rust and using vtable-less loops. worth benchmarking.

DevX: next steps I suggest:
- define minimal runtime contract JSON/bytecode (owner: Chris)
- control-plane compile flow + test harness (owner: Maria)
- caching and signed blob sync design (owner: Sam)
- telemetry fields and debug endpoints (owner: Priya)
- perf benchmark job (owner: Chris/DevX)

Alyssa: thanks. let's sync Wednesday 10am to lock the contract. If no objections by EOD tomorrow we start the impl tickets. :thumbsup:

InfraBot: deploy plan reminder: feature-flag gate for edge eval rollout. will prepare rollout checklist.

DevX: capturing notes in the RFC follow-up doc now. I also added an early sketch of the JSON contract. link: https://rwd-internal/docs/rfcs/policy-edges

Priya: +1. minor nit: include a TTL override per-tenant in contract so support can speed propagation in emergencies.

Alyssa: noted. added as action item.

Sam: ACK.

Chris: ACK.

Maria: ACK.

(End)
